source: Minchat Shai on Gen 34:14 + 34:31 ('אחתנו — three in the Torah, two lean and one full; the Ramah: SHALL-HE-MAKE-OUR-SISTER-AS-A-HARLOT alone is written full vav, all the rest lean; the printer erred and his own Masorah convicts him')
claim_en: THE ONE FULL SISTER: אחותנו is written full with its vav exactly once in the Torah — the brothers' closing cry, 'shall he make OUR SISTER as a harlot?' (34:31); the two lean twins (builder-checked) are Rebecca's send-off blessing (24:60) and the deceit-speech's own 'to give OUR SISTER to one uncircumcised' (34:14). The sister-word is whole only in the verse that refuses her dishonor.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 34:22 ('the Ramah's rule: every circumcise-form — המול, ימול, בהמול, להמול — is written FULL in the Torah, except ONE lean: the להמל of but-in-this-will-we-consent; the Hilleli's lean at 34:22 is an error, all the books full')
claim_en: THE DECEIT'S ONE LEAN LETTER: the Ramah rules every circumcise-form in the Torah written FULL — and the single exception is להמל in the brothers' false offer: 'only in this will we consent... TO BE CIRCUMCISED' (34:15). The covenant-verb of Abraham (17:10), the Passover stranger (Exod 12:48), and even this chapter's own repeats (34:17, 34:22, all builder-checked full) keep their vav; the one spoken in deceit is written one letter short.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 34:5 ('והחרש — lean of yod; the Masorah: two lean in the Torah, Jacob's and the vows-law's; so the Ramah, with his rule for the whole hearing-and-silence language')
claim_en: THE TWO SILENCES: והחרש ('and Jacob KEPT SILENT until they came,' 34:5 — the father's silence over Dinah) is written lean of its yod exactly twice in the Torah; the other is the vows-law's silence — the hearer who says nothing and by silence lets the woman's vow stand (Num 30:12): the silence over the daughter and the silence that binds, spelled as one lean pair.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 34:3 ('את הנער, לב הנער — read הנערה, and so the second and third; the Masorah: all the Torah written lean except one, the fine-verse of Ki Tetzei; the he alone carries the stress-stroke in the precise books')
claim_en: DINAH IN THE BOY'S LETTERS: all three of Dinah's maiden-tokens in this chapter (34:3 twice, 34:12) are written in the bare boy-skeleton הנער and read as the maiden — girl-vowels on boy-letters in the stream (builder-checked), the characterized maiden-law holding (its one written-whole exception remains Deut 22:19); and the SAME skeleton stands once more in this chapter as an actual boy — Shechem himself, 'the YOUNG MAN did not delay' (34:19, boy-vowels, builder-checked): one set of letters carrying the violated maiden and her violator.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 34:27 ('טמאו — three in the Masorah: they DEFILED their sister; they DEFILED My sanctuary (Ezekiel); they DEFILED Your holy temple (Ps 79): all learned from the deed of Shechem')
claim_en: THE DEFILED SISTER, ONCE IN THE TORAH: טמאו ('the sons of Jacob... plundered the city that had DEFILED their sister,' 34:27) — the word's only Torah token; the Masorah's two companions are the defiled sanctuary of Ezekiel and the defiled temple of Psalm 79 (named): the Kitzur reads every later defilement as learned from Shechem's deed — the sister and the sanctuary defiled in one word.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 34:7 ('ויתעצבו — the tzadi DAGESHED; and כשמעם ויתעצבו is one of the VERSES WITHOUT DECISION per R. Tanchuma in the Yerushalmi — whether when-they-heard binds backward or forward has no ruling')
claim_en: THE GRIEF DAGESHED, IN THE VERSE WITHOUT A DECISION: ויתעצבו ('and the men WERE GRIEVED,' 34:7) — the tzadi dageshed as ruled; and the tradition marks this very clause as one of Scripture's verses WITHOUT DECISION (R. Tanchuma's list): whether 'when they heard' leans on the coming home or on the grieving is never ruled — while SNAPSHOT's accent stream, which must sing the verse one way, binds it forward with the pashta on the grief-verb: the instrument committing where the tradition holds the question open.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 34:25 ('שני בני — with MAQQEF, not with galgal, in the precise Sephardic books and early print') + 34:28 ('אשר בעיר — with maqqef and no other accent on אשר')
claim_en: THE JOINING STROKES OF THE SWORD-DAY: at 'the TWO SONS of Jacob, Simeon and Levi' (34:25) the precise Sephardic books rule maqqef (the joining stroke), NOT the wheel-accent — and SNAPSHOT joins them, maqqef in the stream (DB-checked); likewise 'that which was in the city' (34:28) joined bare as ruled: the wheel-vs-stroke question that split at Esau's meeting (33:1, 33:10) lands here on the stroke's side, with the books of Spain.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 34:25 ('בהיותם — the he with SHEVA ALONE, not the printer's compound') + 34:9 ('בנתיכם — the bet dageshed') + 34:31 ('הכזונה — soft kaf, no stress-stroke, per the Michlol; one large-letter alphabet makes the zayin LARGE, but the precise books and the standard lists do not')
claim_en: POINTING AS RULED — AND THE HE HOLDS THE LINE: בהיותם ('on the third day, WHEN THEY WERE in pain,' 34:25) — the he with plain sheva (the silent half-vowel) against the printer's compound: a THIRD guttural witness for the half-vowel law's boundary (after the two ayin stations); בנתיכם ('your daughters,' 34:9) bet dageshed; הכזונה ('as a HARLOT,' 34:31) kaf soft with no stress-stroke as the Michlol rules — its large-zayin question (one alphabet enlarges it; Minchat Shai sides with the precise books against) filed to the uninstrumented letter-size layer.

THE CHAPTER'S MORAL VERDICT IS RECORDED OPEN, WITH BOTH SENTENCES PRESERVED. The father: the barrel was CLEAR and you MUDDIED it - with the rider that these peoples are destined to fall into my hand, but only at six hundred thousand. The sons: the barrel was MUDDIED and WE CLARIFIED it - shall he treat our sister as a harlot? Neither sentence is withdrawn and no verdict is entered. On the hardest chapter in the book the chain declines to rule and files both arguments.

check.note: A moral verdict deliberately left unresolved with both parties' arguments preserved verbatim.

claim_en: THE COVENANT VOCABULARY OF LOVE IS MINED OUT OF THE VIOLATOR'S OWN CLAUSES. The chain states that God loves Israel by three expressions - cleaving, desiring, wanting - AND WE LEARN THEM FROM THE PORTION OF THIS WICKED ONE, taking all three from this chapter's descriptions of the man who assaulted her, with love and speaking-to-the-heart added from the same verses. The most startling register move in the sweep: the words for divine attachment are sourced from a crime scene. The section also states that Israel never puts its finger first into the idolater's mouth - THEY demanded intermarriage first - and fixes the marriage-payment terms.

check.note: Covenant-love vocabulary explicitly sourced from the verses describing an assailant's attachment.

claim_en: A FULL CASE-SHELF DISCUSSION RUNS INTO THE READING AND NAMES THIS VERSE AS ITS MEASURE. On the third-day pain the chain quotes an entire cluster on bathing a circumcised child on the sabbath - whether one bathes the child or only the circumcision, the proof from the rule about oil and hot water on wounds, the third-day allowance, the midwives' standing instruction to do on the sabbath whatever they do on weekdays - and Shmuel's ruling: BECAUSE OF DANGER, OUR VERSE IS THE MEASURE of the third day's peril. A verse-anchored narrative supplying the empirical basis for a sabbath ruling, with the dissent that there is no prohibition here recorded beside it.

check.note: A sabbath ruling on danger taking this narrative verse as its empirical measure, with the permissive dissent preserved.

claim_en: A NAMING RULE IS DERIVED FROM WHOSE BROTHERS THEY ARE CALLED. They are called the sons of Jacob because they took counsel from neither their father nor each other, and DINA'S BROTHERS because they risked themselves for her - from which the rule that one is named for the person one is devoted to, with two further cases named. The chain adds their age at thirteen, and records the father standing at the gate with sword and bow against the deed's consequences - which is where a later verse's boast is seated.

check.note: A naming convention derived from a kinship label, with three cases, plus the father's opposition recorded as an act.

claim_en: THE CHAIN'S OWN VERDICT OSCILLATES BETWEEN ROBBERY AND PRIESTHOOD IN ONE PASSAGE. Asked whether the two acted like waylaying robbers, the answer upgrades them to a COMPANY OF PRIESTS at the threshing floor - entitled rather than predatory - and says outright that it was PROPER for them to have killed in Shekhem, on the ground that she was being treated as ownerless. And in the same breath it asks who caused the whole thing, and answers with her going out. Prosecution and defence in a single section.

check.note: A single passage grading the same act as robbery, as priestly entitlement, and as caused by the victim's own movement.

claim_en: THE DECEIT-WORD IS LIFTED OFF THE BROTHERS BY THE TRANSLATION WHERE THE MIDRASH DEFENDS IT INSTEAD. Onkelos renders their answer as given WITH WISDOM rather than with guile. The chain takes the opposite route, keeping the word and quoting the narrator's own justification clause: do you think there is deceit here? The Divine Spirit says - because he had defiled Dina their sister. The same solving-pattern as the theft at gen_53: one member renames the act, the other keeps the name and supplies the warrant.

check.note: An accusatory term renamed by the translation while the midrash keeps it and cites the narrator's justification.

claim_en: WHOSE CONFIDENCE THE ADVERB DESCRIBES IS DISPUTED ACROSS THE SHELF. The chain reads that the attackers came confident IN THE ELDER'S STRENGTH; Onkelos moves the confidence to the other party, rendering it as the city THAT DWELT SECURELY - unsuspecting rather than emboldened. One adverb, two subjects, and the difference decides whether the verse describes an assault force or its unaware victims.

check.note: A single adverb assigned to opposite subjects by the two members, changing whom the verse describes.

claim_en: THE TRANSLATION FLATTENS EXACTLY THE VERBS THE MIDRASH BUILDS ITS TABLE ON. Where the chain mines cleaving and desiring from these verses to describe divine love, Onkelos renders the assault as MISTREATMENT and the cleaving as mere desire - draining the intensity from the same clauses. The two shelves pull in opposite directions on one sentence: one raises the vocabulary to covenant register, the other lowers it to plain description.

check.note: The translation weakening the precise verbs the midrash elevates into covenant vocabulary, on the same clause.

claim_en: THE DEED IS CARRIED TO A DEATHBED COURT AND JUDGED THERE. The later verdict on the two - brothers, each taking his sword - is read as brothers FOR HER but not for their other brother, and the weapons are called instruments of villainy that belong to Esau rather than to them. This chapter's act is thereby entered as evidence in a judgment delivered fifteen chapters later, in a block not yet derived.

check.note: An act entered as evidence in a later deathbed judgment, with the verdict distinguishing this deed from another.

claim_en: THE AFTERMATH IS SETTLED THREE WAYS AND HER OWN QUESTION IS PRESERVED. Her cry is recorded - and I, where will I carry my shame? - and answered by the claim that one of the brothers took her, with the epithet attached to the son read three ways: that he acted as a Canaanite, that the man was a Hivite within Canaan, or that he BURIED her in Canaan. Her question survives all three answers.

check.note: A victim's recorded question answered three incompatible ways, with the question preserved rather than resolved away.
